question: What chemical reactions occur when the proteins and sugars in and on your food are changed by heat, creating new tastes, aromas, and colors?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Maillard reaction.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Maillard reaction** occur when the proteins and sugars in and on your food are changed by heat, creating new tastes, aromas and colours.
 
• It is a chemical reaction between **amino acids and reducing sugars that gives browned food its distinctive flavour.**
 
• Like caramelization, it is a form of non-enzymatic browning.
 
• It takes place during the cooking of meat.
 
• The reactive carbonyl group of the sugar interacts with the nucleophilic amino group of the amino acid, and interesting but poorly characterized odour and flavour molecules result.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The increase in volume, viscosity, and translucency of starch granules when they are heated in a liquid is called **Gelatinization**.
 
• ​**Dextrinization **is the process involving the browning of starch foods when subjected to dry heat.
 
 
• It is defined as the breakdown of starch into dextrins (disaccharides).
 
 
 
• Caramelization is a slow cooking process that occurs when sugar is cooked over low heat, causing a change in both appearance and flavour.
